messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Name: [Patient Name]
Medical Record Number: [MRN]

Admission Date: [Admission Date]
Discharge Date: [Discharge Date]

History of Present Illness:
The patient, a 53-year-old male with a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus and dyslipidemia, underwent laparoscopic right hemicolectomy with D3 lymphadenectomy for moderately differentiated tubular adenocarcinoma of the ascending colon. Postoperative surveillance revealed a 23-mm sessile polyp at the superior rectum, which was successfully removed by endoscopic mucosal resection. 39 months after EMR, a mass lesion was found in the presacral area on CT as postoperative surveillance. The patient underwent LAR with D3 lymphadenectomy, and the recurrent site was completely removed without adjuvant chemotherapy.

Hospital Course:

Admission:
The patient was admitted for LAR with D3 lymphadenectomy due to presacral lymph node recurrence of rectal cancer.

Treatment:
The patient underwent LAR with D3 lymphadenectomy, and the recurrent site was completely removed by surgery.

Clinical Progress:
The postoperative course was uneventful, and he was discharged from our hospital on postoperative day 11.

Discharge Condition:
The patient was discharged in a stable condition.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Disposition:
The patient was discharged home in stable condition.

Instructions:
The patient should follow up with his primary care physician and oncologist for postoperative surveillance per their recommendations.

Signed,
[Physician Name]
[Title]

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
The admission was for low anterior resection with D3 lymphadenectomy for presacral lymph node recurrence of rectal cancer.

The 23-mm rectal polyp was removed by EMR, and a rectal primary is implied. The recurrence is described as "presacral lymph node recurrence of rectal cancer", which is a metastasis to a lymph node. That would suggest C77 (secondary malignant neoplasm of lymph nodes), but the case could also be coded as a primary rectal malignancy, C20.

In ICD-10-AM, a recurrence of the primary at the same site is coded to the primary site category. A lymph node recurrence is a secondary neoplasm, and secondary sites are coded as C77 when the lymph nodes are the focus of treatment. Here the admission was specifically for the nodal recurrence, with the primary already excised. Strictly, if the primary has been removed and there is no evidence of remaining disease at the primary site, the primary is coded as a personal history (Z85) and the metastasis is coded as principal. The principal diagnosis would therefore be the secondary site, C77.

The presacral area is a retroperitoneal or pelvic nodal region, so it falls under C77.2 (intra-abdominal lymph nodes) or C77.5 (intrapelvic lymph nodes). Either way the category is C77.

**C77**
